tool_analysis:
1. Step Analysis:
The recorded session logs into Magento Admin, navigates to the Manage Customers grid, and demonstrates all relevant mass customer actions:
- Authentication at the admin login page
- Closing an overlay notification popup
- Selecting customers via individual row checkboxes and via Select Visible / Select All
- Using the Actions dropdown to:
  * Assign a customer group (with group dropdown + Submit)
  * Subscribe to newsletter
  * Unsubscribe from newsletter
  * Delete selected customers
- Using Unselect All
- Demonstrating a filter (Group = Wholesale) and Search
- Demonstrating sorting by Email column.
Selectors are anchored via element_hash values and also consistently positioned controls (Actions select, Submit button, selection links, group filter dropdown, Search, column header link). Previous tools failed around agent steps 4–5 due to unstable or ambiguous selectors; this version leans on elementHash for deterministic interactions and avoids over-complicated dynamic logic.

2. Task Definition:
Create a reusable tool that, given a desired mass action and optional selection and filter parameters, will:
- Ensure we are on the Manage Customers grid (logging in if session expired)
- Optionally apply a simple Group filter
- Select customers according to a selection mode (visible only or all records in grid)
- Apply one chosen bulk action from Magento’s Actions dropdown: delete, subscribe, unsubscribe, or assign group.

The demo also showed additional actions (manual subset selection, sorting) but the core single-purpose task is: perform one specified mass action on a chosen customer set in the grid. Sorting and arbitrary filters are not essential to that; they were part of the demonstration only, so they will not be parameterized to keep the tool focused and deterministic.

3. Action Plan:
A. Navigation & Login
- Step 1: navigation to the customer grid URL `/index.php/admin/customer/`.
- Step 2: agentic check: if redirected to login, fill username/password and submit; otherwise, proceed. Because element hashes for login fields are known, but the presence of the login page vs. grid is dynamic, this is best represented as an agent step that handles both cases within a few sub-steps.

B. Ensure we are on the Manage Customers grid
- No extra navigation needed beyond the main URL; once logged in, Magento lands on the requested grid.

C. Optional filter by customer group (simple deterministic case)
- If a `filter_group` parameter is provided (one of General, Wholesale, VIP Member, Private Sales Member), change the Group filter select control and click Search.
- Implement this as deterministic interactions with the filter dropdown elementHash and Search button elementHash. Agent logic is not necessary because these controls are static once on the grid.

D. Selection Mode
- Use parameter `selection_mode` to control which customers to select:
  * `visible`: click the Select Visible link to select all rows on the current page (20 by default).
  * `all`: click Select All to select all records in the (filtered) grid.
- Before selecting, click Unselect All to clear any previous selections, ensuring idempotency.

E. Choose Mass Action
- Use parameter `action` mapped to the Actions dropdown:
  * `delete` → Delete
  * `newsletter_subscribe` → Subscribe to Newsletter
  * `newsletter_unsubscribe` → Unsubscribe from Newsletter
  * `assign_group` → Assign a Customer Group (requires `action_group` parameter)
- Select the appropriate option in the Actions dropdown using a `select_change` step tied to the stable elementHash.

F. For `assign_group` only
- Use the mass-action group dropdown (which appears after choosing Assign a Customer Group) and choose `action_group` (enum: General, Wholesale, VIP Member, Private Sales Member).

G. Submit
- Click the Submit button to execute the bulk operation.

H. Optional confirmation extraction
- Use an extraction step to pull the resulting success/error message (e.g., "Total of X record(s) were updated" or "were deleted") into a context variable `mass_action_result` so callers can verify outcome.

4. Variable Identification:
Inputs that must be parameterized based on the task and recorded steps:
- `username` (string, required=false): Admin username. The demo used `admin`. Usually fixed in this environment, so keep optional with default behaviour up to caller.
- `password` (string, required=false): Admin password. The demo used `password123`. Again, optional to allow overrides.
- `selection_mode` (string enum, required=true): How to select customers for mass action.
  * Allowed: `visible`, `all`.
- `action` (string enum, required=true): Which bulk action to execute.
  * Allowed: `delete`, `newsletter_subscribe`, `newsletter_unsubscribe`, `assign_group`.
- `action_group` (string enum, required=false): Customer group name for `assign_group`. Options seen: `General`, `Wholesale`, `VIP Member`, `Private Sales Member`. Required only when action == assign_group; tool schema will mark it optional but description will explain dependency.
- `filter_group` (string enum, required=false): Group filter option in the grid filter row for narrowing the customer set before selection.
  * Allowed: `Any`, `General`, `Wholesale`, `VIP Member`, `Private Sales Member`. Demo used `Wholesale`.

Other demonstrated behaviors (sorting by Email, filtering by other columns, manually choosing only a couple of customers) aren’t central to performing mass actions generically and introduce complexity and brittleness, so they are excluded from the input schema.

5. Step Optimization & Determinism:
- Navigation is a single deterministic step directly to `/index.php/admin/customer/`; no intermediate clicks through the menu.
- Login is handled in an agent step because the page may or may not be a login form; once logged in, subsequent elements are static.
- All mass-action controls (Select All, Select Visible, Unselect All, Actions dropdown, group dropdown, Submit, Group filter, Search) showed stable element_hash values across multiple interactions and page states, indicating they are reliable.
- Instead of UI-driven complex selection patterns (picking specific IDs as in the demo), selection is parameterized by mode (`visible` vs `all`) which is exactly how Magento’s bulk actions are intended to be used. This simplifies the tool and avoids fragile per-row selectors.
- We do not add URL-manipulation (Pass 2) because Magento’s grid filtering and mass actions are generally POST-based and rely on form keys and CSRF protection; directly editing query parameters would not produce correct POSTs for bulk operations.
- Problematic areas from previous attempts (selectors resolving to multiple elements, inconsistent Submit button selectors) are mitigated by consistently reusing the elementHash values captured for each control and avoiding generic CSS selectors.

Overall the tool now:
- Navigates and logs in if needed
- Optionally filters by customer group
- Clears existing selections, selects the desired customer set
- Applies one chosen mass action, handling the extra group dropdown when needed
- Extracts the Magento success message for verification.

This is strictly focused on the core mass-action behaviour, without extra demo-only filters or sorting.
name: tool_mass_action_customers_v3
description: Perform Magento admin customer grid mass actions (delete, subscribe/unsubscribe newsletter, assign customer group) on selected customers using stable selectors and robust interactions.

steps.description: Navigate directly to the Magento Admin Manage Customers grid URL (will redirect to login if not authenticated).
Handle conditional login vs. already-authenticated state and end on the Manage Customers grid.
steps.task: If the current page is a Magento Admin login form, log in using username '{username}' (or 'admin' if empty) and password '{password}' (or 'password123' if empty), then ensure we are on the Manage Customers grid at /admin/customer/. If already on the Manage Customers grid, do nothing and proceed.

steps.description: Close the incoming message/notification popup if present so that grid controls are not obscured.
Click the 'Unselect All' control to clear any pre-existing selections in the customer grid.

If filter_group is provided, choose the corresponding option in the Group filter dropdown in the grid filter row. If filter_group is empty or 'Any', this should select 'Any' to disable group filtering.
Apply the current grid filters (including Group filter) by clicking the 'Search' button.
Select customers for the mass action: when selection_mode is 'all', click 'Select All'; when 'visible', click 'Select Visible'.
Choose the desired mass action in the Actions dropdown based on the 'action' input: Delete, Subscribe to Newsletter, Unsubscribe from Newsletter, or Assign a Customer Group.
steps.selectedText: {action == "delete" ? "Delete" : (action == "newsletter_subscribe" ? "Subscribe to Newsletter" : (action == "newsletter_unsubscribe" ? "Unsubscribe from Newsletter" : "Assign a Customer Group"))}

steps.description: When action is 'assign_group', select the destination customer group from the mass-action Group dropdown that appears (General, Wholesale, VIP Member, or Private Sales Member). For other actions, this step is effectively a no-op and may be skipped by the executor.
Click the 'Submit' button to execute the selected mass action on the currently selected customers.
Extract the success/error notification text after submitting the mass action so callers can verify the outcome.
steps.goal: Capture the Magento system message summarizing the result of the mass action (e.g., 'Total of X record(s) were updated' or 'Total of X record(s) were deleted.') and any error messages.

input_schema.name: username
input_schema.description: Magento admin username to use on the login page (defaults to 'admin' in this environment if not provided).

input_schema.name: password
input_schema.description: Magento admin password to use on the login page (defaults to 'password123' in this environment if not provided).

input_schema.name: selection_mode
input_schema.description: Which customers to select before running the mass action: 'visible' selects all rows on the current grid page via 'Select Visible'; 'all' selects all records in the (filtered) grid via 'Select All'.

input_schema.name: action
input_schema.description: Which Magento mass action to perform on the selected customers: 'delete' = Delete; 'newsletter_subscribe' = Subscribe to Newsletter; 'newsletter_unsubscribe' = Unsubscribe from Newsletter; 'assign_group' = Assign a Customer Group.

input_schema.name: action_group
input_schema.description: Customer group to assign when action is 'assign_group'. Ignored for other actions.

input_schema.name: filter_group
input_schema.description: Optional Group filter to apply in the customer grid before selection. Uses the Group filter dropdown in the filter row; 'Any' disables group filtering.
